guidelines: Score exactly one chain: take the maximum subtotal among chains; do not add points across chains. This rubric implements this by providing mutually exclusive regimes for the Complex Bashing approach and a comprehensive additive regime for the Synthetic Geometry approach (which also covers all partial progress).
0 points for conjecturing that OM = ON from an accurately drawn diagram without any angle chasing or algebraic proof.
0 points for simply restating the problem or rewriting the given angle conditions without deriving meaningful conclusions (e.g., not finding the tangent conditions).
0 points for the computation part if introducing complex coordinates but failing to simplify them into a usable factored form (e.g., writing the full determinant for O_A but not evaluating it).
0 points for any incomplete computational approach that does not finish the solution, unless it arrives at meaningful synthetic observations (which are then scored under the synthetic chain).

children.description: Prove that triangle ABC is similar to triangle EFD (e.g., by identifying that DE is tangent to (AFE)).
Introduce the Miquel point P of triangle ABC with respect to D, E, F.
Establish that P is the center of a spiral similarity mapping ABC to EFD (may be cited as a standard consequence of the Miquel point).
Prove that triangle ABC is similar to triangle O_A O_B O_C.
Prove that P is the center of a spiral similarity mapping EFD (or ABC) to O_A O_B O_C. (Unjustified assumption of spiral similarity from mere similarity earns 0 for this item).
Deduce that P is the center of a spiral similarity mapping the respective circumcenters M -> N -> O. (Unjustified assumption of spiral similarity from mere similarity earns 0 for this item).

Conclude OM = ON using the properties of paired spiral similarities, explicitly noting why the relevant triangle (e.g., A E O_A) is isosceles. (Incomplete similarity argument missing this justification earns 0 for this item).
